title: Read-only MCP refusals carry error.reminders and error.next like every other tool error
outcome: Read-only MCP refusals carry error.reminders and error.next like every other tool error
acceptance: A refusal from engram mcp --read-only carries error.reminders and error.next, as docs/features/cli-and-mcp.md says every agent tool error does, or that document's Read-only mode section states the exception; a refusal test pins the shape.
The test that compares database and WAL bytes around read-only calls asserts that each read succeeds and the refused write is an isError result, so it fails if the reads refuse.

completion.summary: A refusal from engram mcp --read-only now carries error.reminders (one fixed line naming the restriction, never echoing the caller's input) and error.next (the read to make instead: next --peek, memories, or nothing for undeclared arguments), like every verb error. The refusal test pins both fields for each restriction, the stdio dogfood test checks them, and the database/WAL byte test now asserts that its reads answer and its refused write is a tool error. Landed c0ac723. Round 1 was clean. The full gate test-8f9b4030 passed 9/9 after a restart-interrupted run; the independent evaluation passed 2/2.
